explanations.answer: See the land given to Israel
explanations.explanation: That's the job, friend. The LORD says, "Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites." (Numbers 27:12) Notice the word "given." The land is a gift already handed over, and Moses gets a front-row look at it.

explanations.answer: Build an altar to the LORD
explanations.explanation: I get why an altar comes to mind, since mountains and altars go together in a lot of stories. But this time the LORD sends Moses up for a different reason. He says, "see the land that I have given the Israelites." (Numbers 27:12) No bricks, no stones, just a long look.

Nope, nobody is meeting Moses up there. The text mentions no elders at all. The LORD says, "Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites." (Numbers 27:12) Moses is sent to look, and that's the whole assignment.

Ooh, I know why this one sounds right. A leader walks his people all that way, so you expect him to walk in with them. But God doesn't say that. He says, "After you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was." (Numbers 27:13) Moses sees the land, and that's where his part ends.

Right, and it's a tender one. God doesn't say Moses will lead Israel into the land. He says, "After you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was." (Numbers 27:13) Moses gets to see it, and he is gathered to his people.

Aaron it is. God says Moses will be gathered to his people "as your brother Aaron was." (Numbers 27:13) These two went through a whole lot together, and God ties their endings together in one short line.

Korah is a name from earlier in Numbers, so I see how it floated up. But Korah isn't Moses' brother, and he isn't the one God names here. God says, "as your brother Aaron was." (Numbers 27:13) The word "brother" is your clue.
Caleb is a good name to know, but he isn't the one here. God is talking about Moses' own brother. He says, "as your brother Aaron was." (Numbers 27:13) Same family, same long road.

Yes, and God says it straight. He tells Moses, "both of you rebelled against My command to show My holiness in their sight regarding the waters." (Numbers 27:14) Both of them, Moses and Aaron. The text doesn't soften it, so I won't either.

This one is True, and it's a hard one to hear. God says, "both of you rebelled against My command to show My holiness in their sight regarding the waters." (Numbers 27:14) The "both of you" means Moses and Aaron. God says it plainly, so we take it plainly.

explanations.answer: A man to lead the congregation
explanations.explanation: That's it. Moses has just heard hard news about himself, and his first thought is the people. He asks the LORD to "appoint a man over the congregation." (Numbers 27:16) I think that says a lot about the kind of leader he was.

I bet plenty of us would ask for that one, me first. But Moses doesn't. He asks, "May the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation." (Numbers 27:16) His request is about who leads next, not about himself.

explanations.answer: A way into the land after all
explanations.explanation: Good guess, because that's what a lot of us would beg for. But the text doesn't have Moses asking that. He asks the LORD to "appoint a man over the congregation." (Numbers 27:16) His request is for the people's next leader.

Yes, sheep. Moses says he doesn't want the congregation of the LORD "to be like sheep without a shepherd." (Numbers 27:17) Sheep with nobody out front just wander, and Moses knows it. Years later Jesus sees crowds and uses a picture like that too (Matthew 9:36).

Soldiers is a fair guess, since Israel did have fighting ahead of them. But Moses picks a gentler picture. He says the congregation should not "be like sheep without a shepherd." (Numbers 27:17) Shepherds look after their flock, and I think that's the heart of it.

Travelers fits, I'll give you that, because Israel is definitely on a journey. But Moses uses a different picture. He says, "so that the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd." (Numbers 27:17) It's sheep, friend.
Spirit is right. God calls Joshua "a man with the Spirit in him." (Numbers 27:18) Out of everybody in that camp, that's the description God picks.
Strength is a natural guess, since Joshua is going to lead an army. But that's not the word God uses. He says, "a man with the Spirit in him." (Numbers 27:18) The thing God points to is the Spirit.
Fire sounds mighty dramatic, I'll admit. But God doesn't call Joshua a man with fire in him. He says, "a man with the Spirit in him." (Numbers 27:18) Save the fire for my ovens.
That's the one. God says, "Take Joshua son of Nun, a man with the Spirit in him, and lay your hands on him." (Numbers 27:18) It's a simple act, and Moses does it when the time comes (Numbers 27:23).
Oil does show up elsewhere in Scripture, so it's a smart guess. But God doesn't mention oil here. He says, "lay your hands on him." (Numbers 27:18) Hands, nothing poured.
A staff handoff would make a great picture, wouldn't it? But the text doesn't say that here. God's instruction is, "lay your hands on him." (Numbers 27:18) Moses uses his hands, and that's all.

This one is False, friend. God wants it out in the open. He says, "Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, and commission him in their sight." (Numbers 27:19) Nothing private about it.

Right, False. Nothing happens in a back room here. God tells Moses, "commission him in their sight," with Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation standing there. (Numbers 27:19) Everybody gets to see it.

explanations.answer: So the congregation will obey him
explanations.explanation: That's the reason God gives. He says, "Confer on him some of your authority, so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him." (Numbers 27:20) The authority is how the people will know to follow Joshua.

explanations.answer: So Moses can rest on the mountain
explanations.explanation: The text never says that. God gives a different reason: "so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him." (Numbers 27:20) It's about the people following Joshua. Moses taking a nap doesn't come into it.

explanations.answer: So Joshua can judge every case
explanations.explanation: I see why it sounds right, since leaders handle a lot of cases. But the text doesn't give that reason. God says, "so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him." (Numbers 27:20) The goal is that the people obey.

Counsel, you got it. God says Eleazar "will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim." (Numbers 27:21) So Joshua won't be guessing his way through. Counsel gets sought for him before the LORD.

Mercy is a lovely word, but it's not the one God uses here. He says Eleazar "will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim." (Numbers 27:21) Counsel is guidance for the road ahead.

Blessing is a nice thought, but it's not the word in this verse. God says Eleazar "will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim." (Numbers 27:21) It's counsel, the kind you ask for when a decision is coming.

True, and no stalling. The text says, "Moses did as the LORD had commanded him." (Numbers 27:22) He had just heard hard news about himself, and he still got right to it. I think that's worth noticing.
This one is True. After God finishes speaking, the text says, "Moses did as the LORD had commanded him." (Numbers 27:22) No arguing and no dragging his feet. He takes Joshua and gets it done.
